alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 6 at 8:21PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Exceptional rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused Moderate flooding at the gauge west of Cocoa. The river is
forecast to slowly rise into Major flood stage this weekend and into
early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Friday the stage was 16.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Friday was 16.9 feet.

alerts.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 6 at 1:25AM EST until November 8 at 2:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.areas: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...The beaches of Volusia, Brevard, Indian River, Saint
Lucie and Martin counties.

* WHEN...Through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

advisories.text: Update to the St. Johns River flood warning near Cocoa (9 miles west) in Brevard County: at 8:15 AM Friday the river stood at 16.9 feet, above the 16.0-foot flood stage, and moderate flooding is happening now. NWS now expects the river to keep rising, reach major flood stage this weekend and crest at about 17.1 feet late this weekend into early next week. The warning stays in effect until further notice. At 17.2 feet the Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes impassable, cutting off access to the Mullet Lane and Bass Road area. Do not drive around barricades or through flooded areas, and use caution near the riverbanks.

Update to the St. Johns River flood warning near Cocoa (9 miles west) in Brevard County: at 7:15 PM Friday the river stood at 16.9 feet, above the 16.0-foot flood stage, and moderate flooding is happening now. NWS now expects the river to stay steady at about 16.9 feet and still says major flooding is forecast. The warning stays in effect until further notice. At 17.2 feet the Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes impassable, cutting off access to the Mullet Lane and Bass Road area. Do not drive around barricades or through flooded areas, and use caution near the riverbanks.
